memory_candidates.content: Core-extension test suites resolve their subject script 'deploy-tree-first', so running a suite from the source store still tests the stale deployed copy unless CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store is exported. verify-touched.sh with root '.' runs ./.claude/scripts/tests/run-all.sh, so use it for suite selection and re-run the selection via agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh --only with the override. Unset the override for test-common-lib.sh.

Before committing a phase that adds shell or fixture text, run shellcheck -S warning on the touched files and the deployed check-task-references.sh; neither is covered by a phase's selected suites, and a fixture comment such as 'task 9' or an unused local only surfaces later inside test-deploy-propagation.sh and test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh.

Two jq traps that pass syntax checks and silently corrupt output. (1) Inside a bash single-quoted jq program, a regex written as "[\\t\\u001f]" reaches the regex engine as a literal backslash-u sequence, and the character class then matches the letters u, 0, 1 and f, deleting them from text; write control characters with single jq string escapes ("[\t\u001f]") so jq puts the real characters in the pattern. (2) Arguments to a jq function are evaluated against the function's INPUT: `.value | f(.key)` reads .key from .value (null). Bind first: `.key as $k | .value | f($k)`.

A losslessness gate for a prose migration is cheap to make non-vacuous: record, per migrated item, the source lines it was built from; then require (a) multiset equality between all source lines and (destination-file lines read back from the staged file + recorded item lines), and (b) each item equals its recorded lines joined. A dropped line and a duplicated line both fail, and the gate reads the staged output rather than trusting the parser's own bookkeeping. In this task it caught a real scoping defect on its first stage-layout run.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code Bash tool foreground limit
sapience_notes.value: A foreground Bash call is moved to the background after about 180 seconds even when its timeout parameter is 600000 ms, so a single-call bounded waiter cannot exceed roughly 3 minutes; long local runs need nohup with a captured pid and repeated sub-180-second kill -0 polls.

sapience_notes.subject: agent-system verify-touched.sh
sapience_notes.value: Passing it source-store paths does not make it test source-store edits: with the default root it executes the deployed .claude/scripts/tests copies, and --tree-root pointed at agent-system/extensions/core is refused because a root must contain either a .claude mirror or an agent-system tree.

sapience_notes.subject: state.json roadmap schema
sapience_notes.value: The milestone layer was added as roadmap_milestones[] with nested batches while the flat roadmap_batches/roadmap_notes keys stay defined as the unmigrated-store shape; validate-state.sh Check 13 warns and names migrate-roadmap-to-milestones.sh whenever a flat key is present, and a shared accessor (roadmap-entries-lib.sh) falls back to the flat array only when the roadmap_milestones key is absent, so next-batch suggestion keeps working before a store migrates.

sapience_notes.subject: agent-system roadmap generator
sapience_notes.value: specs/ROADMAP.md is rendered in full from state.json (intro with primary_goals and a milestone status table, one dashboard section per roadmap_milestones entry, rules/conventions/repo context last). A file is classified by one fixed sentinel comment on line 1: the generator overwrites only a file carrying it, creates one only when the store holds a milestone, and refuses every other file as hand-authored, naming migrate-roadmap-to-milestones.sh. This replaced classifying files by their section headers, which could not tell generated text from authored text.

sapience_notes.subject: agent-system migrate-roadmap-to-milestones.sh
sapience_notes.value: The migration from flat roadmap_batches to roadmap_milestones is mechanical only: every flat batch goes unchanged under one neutral milestone M1, and dividing the work into real milestones is left to roadmap-agent, so the judgment/rendering split survives. Its gate is a multiset equality over lines run before any write; an item over its field bound is never truncated but retained whole in a retained-prose file that is never overwritten. On the nvim config repository a dry run measured 30 batches, 30 items placed in state and 11 over-bound items retained.

sapience_notes.subject: agent-system state-write PreToolUse hook
sapience_notes.value: It scans Bash command text and blocks any command that both writes to a path shaped like state.json and mentions active_projects, including a throwaway fixture under the session scratchpad; the whole compound command is refused, so unrelated steps chained in it do not run either. Fixtures written with the Write tool, or under another filename, are not affected.

sapience_notes.subject: agent-system roadmap rollout order
sapience_notes.value: After the core extension is redeployed, any repository whose roadmap file is still hand-authored stops regenerating it: /orchestrate's conclusion step has no approval surface, so it degrades loudly on every run until migrate-roadmap-to-milestones.sh has been run (offered behind one question by /roadmap, /todo and /review). Redeploy and migration therefore have to be done back to back per repository.

sapience_notes.subject: jq regex escapes inside bash single quotes
sapience_notes.value: Doubling the backslash for a unicode escape in a jq regex string is harmless. A pattern written "[\\t\\n\\u001f]+" is handed to the regex engine with a literal backslash-u sequence, and the class matched the plain characters u, 0, 1 and f, silently deleting those letters and digits from rendered text. Regex metacharacter escapes such as \\s need the doubled backslash; character escapes such as \t and \u001f must be single so jq substitutes the real character.
